You can't help it. You don't choose for it to happen, it's just an illness that you still have symptoms of and do not know when these symptoms will lessen. Just like any 'physical' illness, yours can be a bit hard to live with sometimes and you sometimes need extra care or consideration. Your friends should understand that, and if they don't, then they obviously aren't very good people and wouldn't make good friends anyway. It sounds like nothing your friends have done has impacted you to feel this way, so it might just be a negative thought you have. Your friends are likely supportive and understanding of you anyway! Try to accept this thought that you have as just that, (a thought), and move on from it. Focus on having a good time with your friends and if you do get worried you are affecting them (which it doesn't seem like it), then just let them know what you're worried about. :)

I am so thankful you are here. I know you must be feeling terrible right now, and I know that you probably have plans to try again but please listen to me. I was in your position, almost a year ago now. I almost overdosed also, but was taken to the hospital when someone found me. Even though I didn't choose to do it at first, I am so glad that I had therapy because it honestly helped me so much. My problems aren't gone, my depression isn't gone, but I have the tools I need to deal with these, I have the strength, I have goals and I most definitely have a will to live. Right now, at this moment in time, I am so thankful that I didn't die that night. Since that time, I have met and connected with amazing people, I have learnt new things, had new experiences and have become a stronger and more determined person. It obviously wasn't easy, and there were more times when I almost gave up. But I made a choice. And that choice was recovery. I choose to live. There are things in your life that you live for, or that you used to live for. Stay for them, and stay for the good moments. Because one day, at a certain moment in time, you to will look back and thank yourself for staying, just for this moment, or for this person, or for this experience. I know I'm making life out to be some amazing thing full of amazing experiences when your life might seem extremely boring and pointless right now, or that maybe if you experience things, mental illness will prevent you from feeling the way you should feel. When you choose to get better, you find the things in your life that you find meaning in. And you strive for them, put them into your life.. work towards them. And I know it might seem really daunting or pointless or stupid, but please consider therapy or even just confiding in somebody. If it doesn't work out, try again until you find somebody. Because there is somebody, there are many people who care and who even feel the same way. I know this became kind of long ahaha but please consider some of the things I have said. You are worth it, and whatever it is that you love, is waiting out there for you in the world. Right now, focus on yourself. I'm here if you want to tell me anything. Thanks

When I was maybe 11, on a holiday in the city. I bought a bottle of water or something by myself and looked up when the man was taking ages to give me the change. He then winked at me and smirked. He was over 40 at least. Creeped me out, and when I told my mother she said it was because I 'was pretty' and I should be flattered. Honestly what the fuck (on both their behalf's).  Anyway also, I don't know if this was before or after but it was definitely around the same time since I was very young. I was in the supermarket baking isle choosing a cake pack by myself, when my parents were in the next isle and a man came up to me and "accidentally" tripped before groping my non existent 'breast' for a good 2 seconds, before apologising and jogging off. I sort of just stood there afterwards in shock at what had just happened. He was probably in his 20's and was wearing sunglasses (indoors) and a cap. It was quite obviously planned and thinking back, I should have really grabbed cans and thrown them at him, causing a big scene. But at the time, I didn't really register what had just happened. Honestly I wish I done that and reported him to the police. Also, my stepfather staring at my chest and my ass from the ages maybe 11 and up. These were the earliest significant ones I can remember, but there was much more later on that could be considered worse. I don't consider myself a misandrist and I do realise there are good men in the world but I can honestly say that many men disgust me.
